alt_definition: Someone who is sanguine stays confidently hopeful even when the outlook is uncertain. After a poor first match, a sanguine coach still expects the team to reach the final.
When you're ambivalent, you have opposing feelings about the same choice at the same time. You may want the new job's higher pay but dread leaving your friends.
A laconic speaker uses very few words, saying enough without elaborating. Asked how the long trip went, she gave the laconic reply, “Fine,” and unpacked her bag.
A recalcitrant person or animal stubbornly resists rules, control, or efforts to make them cooperate. The recalcitrant mule won't move, no matter how firmly you pull.
Something ineffable is so powerful, beautiful, or extraordinary that words seem unable to capture it. Watching the sunrise from a mountain may leave you silent rather than reaching for a description.
When rain, pain, anger, or another intense force abates, it becomes weaker. You wait for the storm to abate before stepping outside.
To ameliorate a bad situation is to make it less harmful or easier to bear, though not necessarily solve it. Extra buses might ameliorate crowding without eliminating the rush-hour problem.
When an appearance belies the truth, it hides or contradicts what is really there. His calm voice belied his nervousness as his hands shook under the table.
To placate an angry person, you do or give something meant to calm them down. The restaurant offered a free dessert to placate a customer whose order was lost.
To deride someone or something is to mock it as foolish or worthless, usually with open contempt. Critics derided the tiny car until it proved surprisingly practical.
Candor is honest, direct speech that doesn't hide an uncomfortable truth. A friend shows candor by telling you your plan has a serious flaw instead of politely pretending it's perfect.
A penchant is a strong, lasting liking for a particular thing or activity. If your uncle has a penchant for bright shirts, his closet probably glows.
A respite is a welcome short break from pain, difficulty, or tiring work. Ten quiet minutes can offer parents a respite before the children charge back into the room.
The epitome of a quality is the person or thing that displays it in its clearest, most complete form. A perfectly organized desk might be the epitome of neatness.
An anomaly is something that doesn't fit the usual pattern and may need explaining. If every plant grows except one, that struggling plant is an anomaly worth checking.
